boards.title: 10 Late-Night Runs That Explain CUNY Hunter College
boards.description: Hunter College students navigate the Upper East Side's mix of high-end dining and reliable late-night staples. From 24-hour diners to iconic pizza slices, these spots fuel late study sessions and post-class gatherings.

cards.title: Midnight Express Diner
cards.subtitle: 24-Hour Yorkville Staple
cards.notes: Visit this classic diner for a late-night omelet or burger; it has served the neighborhood 24/7 since 1977.
cards.short_summary: A 24-hour diner on the Upper East Side known for its extensive menu and traditional New York atmosphere.
cards.evidence_claim: Midnight Express Diner is open 24 hours a day, 7 days a week, and has been serving the neighborhood since 1977.
cards.source_title: Midnight Express Diner | New York NY - Facebook
cards.access_notes: Open 24/7 for dine-in and takeout.

cards.title: 7th Street Burger
cards.subtitle: Late-Night Smashburgers
cards.notes: Stop by for a simple, high-quality smashburger; the Upper East Side location stays open until 3:00 AM on weekends.
cards.short_summary: A popular NYC smashburger chain known for its focused menu and late-night availability near campus.
cards.evidence_claim: The 7th Street Burger location at 1603 2nd Ave is open until 3:00 AM on Wednesday through Saturday.
cards.source_title: Perfect Cheeseburger in Upper East Side | 7th Street Burger
cards.access_notes: Open until 3:00 AM Wednesday-Saturday; until midnight other days.

cards.title: Insomnia Cookies
cards.subtitle: Warm Cookies Until 3 AM
cards.notes: Order warm cookies for a late-night study break; this location delivers and serves in-store until 3:00 AM on weekends.
cards.short_summary: A late-night bakery chain specializing in warm cookies, popular for delivery to dorms and libraries.
cards.evidence_claim: Insomnia Cookies on 2nd Ave is open until 3:00 AM on Thursday, Friday, and Saturday.
cards.source_title: Insomnia Cookies | Warm Cookie Delivery & Baked Treats Until Late Night
cards.access_notes: Open until 3:00 AM Thursday-Saturday; until 1:00 AM Sunday-Wednesday.

cards.title: Mansion Diner
cards.subtitle: Historic Neighborhood Eatery
cards.notes: Grab a booth at this historic diner, featured in 'Only Murders in the Building,' open until 1:00 AM on weekends.
cards.short_summary: A family-owned diner serving the Upper East Side since 1945 with a classic American menu.
cards.evidence_claim: Mansion Diner is open until 1:00 AM on Friday and Saturday, and until midnight on other days.
cards.source_title: Mansion Diner: Home
cards.access_notes: Open until 1:00 AM Friday-Saturday; 12:00 AM Sunday-Thursday.

cards.title: Joe's Pizza
cards.subtitle: Iconic Late-Night Slice
cards.notes: Take a short trip to 14th Street for a quintessential NYC slice; this location serves until 4:00 AM or later.
cards.short_summary: A legendary New York pizzeria known for its thin-crust slices and late-night service.
cards.evidence_claim: The Joe's Pizza location at 150 East 14th Street is open until 4:00 AM daily.
cards.source_title: Locations — Joe's Pizza
cards.access_notes: Open until 4:00 AM or 5:00 AM daily.

cards.title: The Halal Guys
cards.subtitle: Original Halal Cart
cards.notes: Join the line at the original 53rd Street cart for chicken and rice with famous white sauce, open until 4:00 AM.
cards.short_summary: The world-famous halal food cart that started as a street vendor and now serves late-night crowds daily.
cards.evidence_claim: The Halal Guys cart at W 53rd St and 6th Ave is open until 4:00 AM daily.
cards.source_title: New York, NY | The Halal Guys
cards.access_notes: Open until 4:00 AM daily.

cards.title: Dunkin'
cards.subtitle: 24-Hour Coffee Run
cards.notes: Fuel your all-nighter with coffee and donuts at this 24-hour location just a few blocks south of campus.
cards.short_summary: A reliable 24-hour coffee and donut shop located near the Hunter College campus.
cards.evidence_claim: The Dunkin' at 882 Lexington Ave (near 66th St) is listed as a 24-hour location in official directories.
cards.source_title: Dunkin' locations in New York
cards.access_notes: Open 24 hours daily.

cards.title: McDonald's
cards.subtitle: 24-Hour Fast Food
cards.notes: Head to 1st Avenue for a late-night McFlurry or fries at this 24-hour fast-food staple.
cards.short_summary: A 24-hour McDonald's location providing consistent late-night food options on the Upper East Side.
cards.evidence_claim: The McDonald's at 1279 1st Ave is open 24 hours a day.
cards.source_title: McDonald's 1279 1st Ave NYC
cards.access_notes: Open 24 hours daily.

cards.title: Hunter Deli
cards.subtitle: Campus-Adjacent Bodega
cards.notes: Grab a classic bacon, egg, and cheese or a sandwich at this deli located directly across from the North Building.
cards.short_summary: A popular deli and bodega for Hunter students, offering a wide range of quick meals and snacks.
cards.evidence_claim: Hunter Deli at 966 Lexington Ave is a primary food source for students, located right by the 68th St station.
cards.source_title: Hunter Deli :: Best American in New York
cards.access_notes: Open daily; typically closes around 10:00 PM or 11:00 PM.

cards.title: Wasi's Food Truck
cards.subtitle: North Building Halal Cart
cards.notes: Visit this campus landmark for chicken over rice; it's a ritual for many students between or after classes.
cards.short_summary: A beloved halal food truck parked outside Hunter College's North Building, known for its friendly service.
cards.evidence_claim: Wasi's Food Truck is a recognized campus landmark for Hunter College students, serving breakfast and lunch classics.
cards.source_title: Wasi's Food Truck – Food Atlas of New York
cards.access_notes: Located outside the North Building; hours vary by day but typically serves through the evening.

boards.title: What the Campus Tour Skips: 10 Places Students Share With Each Other
boards.description: Navigate the vertical campus of Hunter College with these student-favored study spots, lounges, and transit-friendly corners across the Upper East Side and beyond.

cards.title: The Silent Reading Room
cards.subtitle: East Building Basement 2
cards.notes: Head to the lowest level of the library for absolute silence. It is a dedicated quiet zone perfect for deep focus during finals week.
cards.short_summary: A subterranean silent study floor in the Leon & Toby Cooperman Library.
cards.evidence_claim: Floor B2 of the Cooperman Library is designated as a Reading Room for silent study.
cards.source_title: Leon & Toby Cooperman Library - Hunter College Libraries
cards.access_notes: Accessible via East Building elevators or stairs; requires Hunter OneCard for entry.

cards.title: Sunset Views on the 7th Floor
cards.subtitle: Connecting West and East Buildings
cards.notes: Use the 3rd and 7th floor bridges to cross Lexington Avenue without leaving the building. The 7th floor offers great sunset views.
cards.short_summary: Enclosed pedestrian bridges connecting the main campus buildings over Lexington Avenue.
cards.evidence_claim: Sky bridges connect the West and East buildings on the 3rd and 7th floors.
cards.source_title: 68th Street Campus Map - Hunter College
cards.access_notes: Open during standard building hours; primary thoroughfare for students moving between classes.

cards.title: Escalator-Side Touchdown Spots
cards.subtitle: West Building Floors 3-7
cards.notes: Find these renovated seating areas next to the escalators on every floor of the West Building for quick study sessions between classes.
cards.short_summary: Renovated student lounges located adjacent to the escalators in the West Building.
cards.evidence_claim: Newly renovated lounges on each floor of the West Building provide spaces for students to touch down between classes.
cards.source_title: Study and Hang Out - Student Living Guide
cards.access_notes: Open during building hours; features various seating arrangements for quiet study or socializing.

cards.title: Sky-High Art Study
cards.subtitle: North Building 16th Floor
cards.notes: Visit the 16th floor for a quiet, specialized library with impressive views of Manhattan. It is often less crowded than the main library.
cards.short_summary: A specialized art library located on the top floor of the North Building.
cards.evidence_claim: The Zabar Art Library is located on the 16th floor of the North Building and is open to all Hunter students.
cards.source_title: Zabar Art Library - Hunter College Libraries
cards.access_notes: Take the North Building elevators to the 16th floor; check library website for specific hours.

cards.title: The Student Union Hangout
cards.subtitle: Thomas Hunter Hall 2nd Floor
cards.notes: Take a break from classes in the game room located within the Student Union. It is a rare dedicated recreational space on campus.
cards.short_summary: A recreational game room for students located in Thomas Hunter Hall.
cards.evidence_claim: Thomas Hunter Hall features a game room and student union on the 2nd floor.
cards.source_title: Student Living Guide - Hunter College
cards.access_notes: Accessible via the 3rd floor sky bridge or the 68th Street entrance.

cards.title: The Tech-Ready Cafe
cards.subtitle: East Building 3rd Floor
cards.notes: Located just outside the library, these booths allow you to plug in your laptop and work while you eat. Perfect for group projects.
cards.short_summary: Technology-equipped study booths located in the East Building.
cards.evidence_claim: Digital Diner Booths are located on the 3rd floor of the East Building outside the Cooperman Library.
cards.source_title: Student Living Guide - Hunter College
cards.access_notes: Open access area; no reservation required but booths fill up quickly during peak hours.

cards.title: The Arts Student Hub
cards.subtitle: Baker Theatre Building 3rd Floor
cards.notes: Relax on colorful couches in this lounge near the theater department. It is a quieter alternative to the main West Building lounges.
cards.short_summary: A student lounge with colorful seating located in the Baker Theatre Building.
cards.evidence_claim: The Gruber Lounge is located on the 3rd floor of the Baker Theatre Building, accessible from the West Building walkway.
cards.source_title: Theatre Facilities - Hunter College
cards.access_notes: Walk through the 3rd floor West Building corridor toward the library and turn right into the Baker Building.

cards.title: East Harlem Escape
cards.subtitle: Silberman School of Social Work
cards.notes: If you are at the East Harlem campus, use the outdoor terrace to escape the city noise. It offers a green reprieve for social work students.
cards.short_summary: An outdoor terrace space at the Silberman School of Social Work campus.
cards.evidence_claim: The Silberman Building features an outdoor terrace for students to eat and study.
cards.source_title: Student Living Guide - Hunter College
cards.access_notes: Located at 2180 Third Avenue; requires Hunter OneCard for building access.

cards.title: Historic Policy Hub
cards.subtitle: 47-49 East 65th Street
cards.notes: Attend a free public lecture or join the Student Ambassador program at FDR's former home. It is a premier site for human rights studies.
cards.short_summary: The historic home of Franklin and Eleanor Roosevelt, now a public policy institute for Hunter College.
cards.evidence_claim: Roosevelt House hosts Hunter undergraduate programs and free public lectures throughout the year.
cards.source_title: Student Orientation to Roosevelt House
cards.access_notes: Open 7 AM - 11 PM for approved spaces; located a few blocks south of the main campus.

cards.title: The Commuter's Secret Entry
cards.subtitle: 68th St - Hunter College Station
cards.notes: Avoid the street-level crowds by entering the West Building directly from the 6 train mezzanine. It is the fastest way to class on rainy days.
cards.short_summary: A direct entrance to the Hunter College West Building from the NYC subway station.
cards.evidence_claim: The West Building can be accessed directly from the subway mezzanine of the 68th Street - Hunter College station.
cards.source_title: Navigating Hunter: Updated Campus Access Plan
cards.access_notes: Requires Hunter OneCard for turnstile entry; open during standard campus hours.

boards.title: Zero Dollars: 10 Hangs That Cost Nothing
boards.description: Discover free social spaces and activities at Hunter College, from sky-high terraces and art galleries to historic libraries and student lounges.

cards.entity_name: Bertha and Karl Leubsdorf Art Gallery
cards.title: Browse Contemporary Art
cards.subtitle: West Building Lobby
cards.notes: Visit this professional gallery on the ground floor for rotating historical and scholarly exhibitions. It is free and open to the public Tuesday through Saturday.
cards.short_summary: A free on-campus art gallery featuring scholarly exhibitions and BFA degree shows.
cards.evidence_claim: All Hunter College Art Galleries are free to visit and open to the public.
cards.source_title: Visit - Hunter College Art Galleries
cards.access_notes: Open Tuesday–Saturday, 12:00 PM – 6:00 PM. Located in the West Building lobby.

cards.title: Walk the Sky Bridges
cards.subtitle: 3rd and 7th Floors
cards.notes: Cross between the East and West buildings while enjoying elevated views of Lexington Avenue. These glass-walled walkways are iconic campus social hubs.
cards.short_summary: Elevated glass walkways connecting the main campus buildings with city views.
cards.evidence_claim: The sky bridges connect the East and West buildings on the 3rd and 7th floors.
cards.source_title: 68th Street Campus Map - Hunter College
cards.access_notes: Accessible during building hours via the 3rd and 7th floors of East and West buildings.

cards.title: Attend a Policy Discussion
cards.subtitle: 47-49 East 65th Street
cards.notes: Join free public programs, film screenings, and lectures at the historic former home of Franklin and Eleanor Roosevelt. Advance registration is required.
cards.short_summary: Free public lectures and programs hosted in the historic Roosevelt House.
cards.evidence_claim: Public Programs at Roosevelt House are free to the public and open with advance registration.
cards.source_title: Upcoming Public Programs - Roosevelt House
cards.access_notes: Free with advance online registration. Located off-campus on East 65th Street.

cards.title: Study in the Art Library
cards.subtitle: North Building, 16th Floor
cards.notes: Relax in upholstered window seats with skyline views. This specialized library offers a quiet, aesthetic space for art and film students to gather.
cards.short_summary: A specialized art library on the 16th floor with casual seating and city views.
cards.evidence_claim: Casual upholstered window seats frame views of the city skyline in the Zabar Art Library.
cards.source_title: Zabar Art Library | Hunter College Libraries
cards.access_notes: Open to CUNY students with valid ID. Check library website for seasonal hours.

cards.title: Relax on the Outdoor Terrace
cards.subtitle: West Building, Room 303
cards.notes: Escape the city noise at this outdoor terrace featuring plants and seating. It is located directly off the main cafeteria for easy access.
cards.short_summary: An outdoor terrace with greenery and tables located on the 3rd floor of the West Building.
cards.evidence_claim: The West Building terrace offers a spacious reprieve with tables and chairs–ideal for studying or socializing.
cards.source_title: Student Living Guide - Hunter College
cards.access_notes: Accessible through the 3rd-floor cafeteria during building hours.

cards.title: Grab a Free Performance Ticket
cards.subtitle: 68th Street Campus
cards.notes: Pick up one free ticket per Hunter ID at the box office on the day of select shows. Performances range from jazz concerts to theatrical productions.
cards.short_summary: Free same-day tickets for Hunter students to select performances at the Kaye Playhouse.
cards.evidence_claim: Students can pick up one free ticket per Hunter ID at the Kaye box office between noon and 6 pm the day of the show.
cards.source_title: American Voices — Frank Sinatra | Hunter College
cards.access_notes: Box office is open Wednesday–Friday, 12:00 PM – 6:00 PM. Tickets are subject to availability.

cards.title: Play in the Game Room
cards.subtitle: Thomas Hunter Hall, Room 205
cards.notes: Head to the 2nd floor for a dedicated social space featuring games and lounge seating. It is a popular spot for students to unwind between classes.
cards.short_summary: A student social space in Thomas Hunter Hall featuring games and lounge areas.
cards.evidence_claim: Thomas Hunter Hall features a game room in Room 205.
cards.source_title: Student Living Guide - Hunter College
cards.access_notes: Open to students during building hours. Located on the 2nd floor.

cards.title: Visit the Historic Library
cards.subtitle: Roosevelt House, 2nd Floor
cards.notes: Study or relax in this beautifully restored historic library. It serves as a quiet student space within the Roosevelt House Public Policy Institute.
cards.short_summary: A historic student library and lounge space located inside the Roosevelt House.
cards.evidence_claim: The historic Sara Delano Roosevelt Library is a student space on the 2nd floor of the Roosevelt House.
cards.source_title: Student Activities - Roosevelt House
cards.access_notes: Open to Hunter students involved with Roosevelt House programs or by appointment.

cards.title: Hang Out in the Miller Lounge
cards.subtitle: West Building, 7th Floor
cards.notes: Find a seat in this spacious lounge located across from Room 714. It is a designated 'Talking Space' where students can socialize or take online classes.
cards.short_summary: A large student lounge on the 7th floor of the West Building designated for social use.
cards.evidence_claim: Sidney Miller Lounge is a 7th Floor Lounge across from Room 714 in the West Building.
cards.source_title: Student Living Guide - Hunter College
cards.access_notes: Open during building hours. Designated as a 'Talking Study Space'.

cards.title: Picnic at Sheep Meadow
cards.subtitle: Central Park West Side
cards.notes: Walk three blocks west to Central Park's premier lawn for sunbathing and picnicking. This 15-acre space offers iconic views of the Manhattan skyline.
cards.short_summary: A massive public lawn in Central Park located just a short walk from the Hunter campus.
cards.evidence_claim: Sheep Meadow is a 15-acre lawn ideal for relaxing, sunbathing, reading, and picnicking.
cards.source_title: Sheep Meadow | Central Park Conservancy
cards.access_notes: Free and open to the public daily from 11:00 AM until dusk, weather permitting.

boards.title: Claimed by 9am: 10 Study Spots Worth Showing Up Early For
boards.description: Navigate the vertical campus of Hunter College with these ten distinct study environments, from silent library basements to sunlit lounges and specialized research centers.

cards.title: Silent Reading Room
cards.subtitle: East Building Basement Level 2
cards.notes: Head to the lowest level of the library for a strictly silent environment. This floor features individual cubicles and desks designed for deep focus without distractions.
cards.short_summary: A dedicated silent study floor located in the second basement level of the Cooperman Library.
cards.evidence_claim: The Cooperman Library has designated floors B1 and B2 as completely silent study areas with no talking or phone conversations permitted.
cards.source_title: Group Study-Noise Policy - Hunter College Libraries
cards.access_notes: Open during library hours; requires a valid Hunter College ID for entry to the East Building.

cards.title: Tech-Enabled Study Rooms
cards.subtitle: East Building Floor 5
cards.notes: Reserve one of the six newly renovated rooms (520-525) for up to two hours. These spaces include wireless display monitors for collaborative digital work.
cards.short_summary: Renovated reservable group study rooms equipped with wireless monitors on the library's 5th floor.
cards.evidence_claim: Rooms 520, 521, 522, 523, 524, and 525 are available for reservation and equipped with display monitors for wireless device connection.
cards.source_title: 5th Floor Study Rooms Available for Reservations - Hunter College Libraries
cards.access_notes: Reservations required via the online system; keys must be picked up from the 3rd-floor circulation desk.

cards.title: The 16th Floor Retreat
cards.subtitle: North Building Room 1608
cards.notes: Take the A5 elevator to the 16th floor for a specialized study space. It offers silent study areas, color printing, and a collection of art history reference works.
cards.short_summary: A specialized library on the 16th floor of the North Building offering silent study and art resources.
cards.evidence_claim: The Zabar Art Library includes silent study areas, outlets, charging stations, and laptops for check-out on the 16th floor of the North Building.
cards.source_title: Zabar Art Library - Hunter College Libraries
cards.access_notes: Accessible via North Building A5 elevator; check specific library hours for 16th-floor access.

cards.title: 7th Floor Social Study
cards.subtitle: West Building Floor 7
cards.notes: Located across from Room 714, this lounge provides a space for 'talking study.' It is ideal for students who need to participate in online classes with headphones.
cards.short_summary: A designated 'Talking Study Space' in the West Building for students attending online classes.
cards.evidence_claim: The Sidney Miller Lounge on the 7th floor of the West Building is a dedicated student Talking Space for taking online courses.
cards.source_title: Student Living Guide - Hunter College
cards.access_notes: Open during building hours; no reservation required.

cards.title: Historic Policy Study
cards.subtitle: Roosevelt House Floor 2
cards.notes: Study in the former personal library of Sara Delano Roosevelt. This historic space is open to students taking public policy or human rights courses at the institute.
cards.short_summary: A historic student study center located within the Roosevelt House Public Policy Institute.
cards.evidence_claim: The SDR Library serves as a student study center for students taking classes at Roosevelt House in public policy and human rights courses.
cards.source_title: Sara Delano Roosevelt Library - Roosevelt House
cards.access_notes: Located at 47-49 East 65th Street; primarily for students enrolled in Roosevelt House programs.

cards.title: Outdoor Lexington View
cards.subtitle: West Building Floor 3
cards.notes: Escape the indoors at this 3rd-floor patio located within the cafeteria. It features tables and chairs with views of Lexington Avenue, perfect for fair-weather studying.
cards.short_summary: An outdoor patio space attached to the West Building cafeteria for studying and dining.
cards.evidence_claim: The West Building terrace offers a spacious reprieve with tables and chairs, ideal for studying or eating with a view of Lexington Avenue.
cards.source_title: Student Living Guide - Hunter College
cards.access_notes: Accessible through the 3rd-floor cafeteria; weather permitting.

cards.title: Social Work Study Hub
cards.subtitle: Silberman Building Floor 1
cards.notes: Visit the East Harlem campus for a change of pace. This library offers four reservable group study rooms and dedicated silent study areas for focused work.
cards.short_summary: The main reading room and study area for the Social Work & Urban Public Health Library.
cards.evidence_claim: The library has four reservable group study rooms, as well as group and silent study areas, located on the main floor of the Silberman Building.
cards.source_title: Social Work & Urban Public Health Library
cards.access_notes: Located at 2180 Third Avenue (119th St); requires Hunter ID for entry.

cards.title: Quiet Stacks at Brookdale
cards.subtitle: Brookdale Campus
cards.notes: For maximum quiet, travel to the Brookdale campus. The library stacks are known among students for being less crowded and very silent compared to the main 68th St campus.
cards.short_summary: A quiet study area located within the Health Professions Library at the Brookdale Campus.
cards.evidence_claim: The Health Professions Library at the Brookdale campus offers quiet study spaces and is often cited by students as a quieter alternative to the main campus.
cards.source_title: Health Professions Library - Hunter College Libraries
cards.access_notes: Located at 425 East 25th Street; requires Hunter ID for entry.

cards.title: Escalator-Adjacent Lounges
cards.subtitle: West Building Floors 3-7
cards.notes: Utilize the renovated 'touch down' spaces located next to the escalators on floors 3 through 7. Each floor features different seating arrangements for quick study sessions.
cards.short_summary: Renovated student lounges located on multiple floors of the West Building for study and socializing.
cards.evidence_claim: Newly renovated lounges are available on every floor of the West Building (3-7), featuring seating conducive to both quiet study and socializing.
cards.source_title: Student Lounges - Hunter College
cards.access_notes: Open access for students during building hours; no reservation required.

cards.title: Academic Support Hub
cards.subtitle: East Building Floor 7
cards.notes: Study in the heart of academic support. This 7th-floor library space houses the Writing, Math, and Science learning centers, offering a productive, resource-rich environment.
cards.short_summary: A centralized academic support and study area on the 7th floor of the Cooperman Library.
cards.evidence_claim: The Silverstein Student Success Center on the 7th floor of the Cooperman Library houses the Writing, Math, and Science Learning Centers.
cards.source_title: About the Hunter College Libraries
cards.access_notes: Accessible via the library's 7th-floor entrance; check center-specific hours for tutoring services.

boards.title: 10 Blocks Off Campus, One Reason Each
boards.description: Navigate the Upper East Side streets surrounding Hunter College, from essential transit hubs and student-led public spaces to the corridors where commuters find quick meals and study spots.

cards.title: The Main Campus Hub
cards.subtitle: Lexington Avenue Corridor
cards.notes: Enter the West Building directly from the 68th Street-Hunter College subway station to reach the skywalks connecting the main campus buildings.
cards.short_summary: The primary intersection for Hunter College, serving as the main entry point for thousands of commuting students via the 6 train.
cards.evidence_claim: The main campus for the school runs between Park and Third avenues, and 67th and 69th streets. Most student activities and classes take place in two high rises at the intersection of Lexington Avenue and 68th Street.
cards.source_title: From Parking To Park: Hunter Students Want Curbside Hangout Space - Streetsblog New York City
cards.access_notes: Public street intersection with direct subway access into the Hunter College West Building.

cards.title: Student-Led Public Space
cards.subtitle: East 69th Street Corridor
cards.notes: Visit this pedestrian-friendly installation outside the North Building, featuring seating and planters designed by the student Placemakers Club.
cards.short_summary: A student-initiated 'Street Seats' project that transformed curbside space into a public gathering area for study and connection.
cards.evidence_claim: New York City is moving forward to transform a stretch of East 69th Street into a vibrant public gathering space... outside Hunter's North Building into a pedestrian-friendly 'Street Seats' installation.
cards.source_title: Hunter Students' Plan for Outdoor Public Seating Gets City Go-Ahead
cards.access_notes: Outdoor public seating area located between Park and Lexington Avenues.

cards.title: Quick Eats for Commuters
cards.subtitle: Third Avenue Corridor
cards.notes: Head to this corridor for reliable quick-service options like Just Salad and Chipotle, popular for students with short gaps between classes.
cards.short_summary: A major commercial avenue east of campus known for its density of fast-casual restaurants and student-friendly dining discounts.
cards.evidence_claim: There is a Just Salad and other quick restaurants on 3rd Avenue and 68th... Chipotle (1153 3rd Avenue) is also listed as a place to eat near Hunter.
cards.source_title: Student Living Guide - Hunter College - CUNY
cards.access_notes: Commercial street with various business hours; many offer discounts with a valid Hunter ID.

cards.title: Historic Arts Landmark
cards.subtitle: Park Avenue Corridor
cards.notes: Explore this landmarked building for contemporary art installations and historic period rooms, located just one block west of the main campus.
cards.short_summary: A historic 19th-century armory repurposed as a premier alternative arts space, offering student ticket rates for exhibitions.
cards.evidence_claim: The Park Avenue Armory is located at 643 Park Ave between 66th and 67th Sts. It offers student prices of $12 for its contemporary projects and historic rooms.
cards.source_title: Park Avenue Armory | Things to do in Lenox Hill, New York Kids - Time Out
cards.access_notes: Open Tuesday-Sunday with varying hours; student ID required for discounted admission.

cards.title: Affordable Retail Corridor
cards.subtitle: Lexington Avenue Corridor
cards.notes: Walk south from campus to find specialized boutiques and affordable shops that distinguish this stretch from the more touristy Fifth Avenue.
cards.short_summary: A commercial stretch south of 68th Street featuring a mix of local delis, shoe stores, and gift shops frequented by the campus community.
cards.evidence_claim: Lexington Avenue is known primarily for its unique and more affordable shopping... the 20-block stretch from 50th to 69th street houses a variety of small stores.
cards.source_title: Lexington Avenue, New York - GPSmyCity
cards.access_notes: Public commercial avenue; most shops operate during standard daytime retail hours.

cards.title: Campus Southern Edge
cards.subtitle: East 67th Street Corridor
cards.notes: Navigate the southern boundary of the main campus near the Baker Building, where students transition between academic halls and local delis.
cards.short_summary: The block housing the Baker Building, marking the southern extent of Hunter's primary four-building complex on the Upper East Side.
cards.evidence_claim: The main campus for the school runs between Park and Third avenues, and 67th and 69th streets... the 67th Street (Baker Building) entrance is mentioned in campus access plans.
cards.source_title: Navigating Hunter: Updated Campus Access Plan Effective March 30 - Hunter College
cards.access_notes: Public street; campus building access requires a valid Hunter ID.

cards.title: Neighborhood Dinner Destination
cards.subtitle: Second Avenue Corridor
cards.notes: Walk a few blocks east to find sit-down Italian restaurants and cafes that serve as the primary dinner spots for the local neighborhood.
cards.short_summary: A corridor located several blocks east of campus, offering a higher concentration of full-service dining options compared to the immediate campus blocks.
cards.evidence_claim: Second and Third Avenues, five to ten blocks north, is where the neighborhood does dinner... Mediterraneo is located at Second Avenue & East 66th Street.
cards.source_title: Hunter College Guide: Best Restaurants, Bars & Hotels Near Campus (2026) | RoamRecs
cards.access_notes: Public avenue with numerous restaurants; most open for lunch and dinner daily.

cards.title: Neo-Grec Brownstone Row
cards.subtitle: East 69th Street Corridor
cards.notes: Observe the remarkably intact row of 19th-century brownstones and the Hungarian Church located just east of the North Building.
cards.short_summary: A National Register Historic District featuring Neo-Grec style architecture that provides a quiet, residential contrast to the high-rise campus.
cards.evidence_claim: The rowhouses numbered 322 to 344 and the Hungarian Church at 346 East 69th Street compose The East 69th Street Historic District of the National Register of Historic Places.
cards.source_title: A Walking Tour of Historic East 69th Street - Our Town NY
cards.access_notes: Public residential street; architectural viewing from the sidewalk is free.

cards.title: High-End Cultural Corridor
cards.subtitle: Madison Avenue Corridor
cards.notes: Walk two blocks west to Madison Avenue to access high-end boutiques and the southern approach to the city's famous Museum Mile.
cards.short_summary: A prestigious avenue west of campus known for luxury retail and its proximity to major cultural institutions like the Frick Collection.
cards.evidence_claim: Madison Avenue is mentioned as a more touristy neighbor to Lexington... with high-end spots like La Duree located at Madison and 70th/71st.
cards.source_title: good spots nearby⁉️ : r/HunterCollege - Reddit
cards.access_notes: Public commercial avenue; luxury retail hours typically 10 AM to 6 PM.

cards.title: Campus Pocket Park
cards.subtitle: East 68th Street Corridor
cards.notes: Utilize this small outdoor plaza between Lexington and Third Avenues for a quick breath of air between lectures.
cards.short_summary: A designated outdoor space on 68th Street that serves as one of the few open-air gathering spots for the dense urban campus.
cards.evidence_claim: Poses Park (68th St. bet. Lexington & 3rd Aves.) is listed as an outdoor space around campus for students.
cards.source_title: Student Living Guide - Hunter College - CUNY
cards.access_notes: Outdoor public plaza; accessible during daylight hours.

boards.title: Only Happens Here: 10 Traditions That Make No Sense Anywhere Else
boards.description: Explore the unique rituals, historic symbols, and student-led traditions that define the Hunter College experience in the heart of Manhattan.

cards.title: The Care of the Future is Mine
cards.subtitle: Official College Motto
cards.notes: Adopted in 1870, this Latin motto appears on the college seal and is a central theme during convocation and commencement ceremonies.
cards.short_summary: The official Latin motto of Hunter College, emphasizing the institution's commitment to education and the future.
cards.evidence_claim: Hunter's motto, Mihi cura futuri (Latin), translates to "The care of the future is mine."
cards.source_title: Hunter College - Wikipedia
cards.access_notes: Visible on the college seal and official documents across campus.

cards.title: The Purple and Gold Spirit
cards.subtitle: Official School Colors
cards.notes: Students and the Spirit Squad wear these colors to represent Hunter pride at athletic events and the annual Alumni Weekend.
cards.short_summary: The official colors of Hunter College, used in regalia, athletics, and campus branding.
cards.evidence_claim: Hunter's official colors are purple and gold, represented by the Purple and Gold Spirit Squad.
cards.source_title: Purple and Gold Spirit Squad - Hunter College - CUNY
cards.access_notes: Colors are prominently displayed during campus events and on official merchandise.

cards.title: The Wistarion Yearbook
cards.subtitle: Named After the Official Flower
cards.notes: Named for the wisteria that once covered the 68th Street building, this yearbook has documented student life for decades.
cards.short_summary: The official yearbook of Hunter College, named after the wisteria flower.
cards.evidence_claim: The yearbook name, Wistarion, stems from Hunter's official flower, the wistaria.
cards.source_title: 80 Years at Hunter: A Look Into The Photo Archives - The Envoy
cards.access_notes: Archived copies are available for viewing at the Hunter College Libraries.

cards.title: The Hunter Hawk
cards.subtitle: Official Athletic Mascot
cards.notes: The Hawk represents Hunter's NCAA Division III teams and is the namesake for student media like Hawk Productions.
cards.short_summary: The official mascot of Hunter College athletics, symbolizing the school's competitive spirit.
cards.evidence_claim: Hunter College's nickname is the Hawks, and the mascot is the Hunter Hawk.
cards.source_title: Hall of Fame - Hunter College Athletics
cards.access_notes: The mascot appears at home games in the Sportsplex and during campus celebrations.

cards.title: Alumni Hall of Fame Induction
cards.subtitle: Honoring Distinguished Graduates
cards.notes: Plaques in the West Lobby honor alumni who have demonstrated outstanding service and leadership in their fields.
cards.short_summary: A tradition of honoring notable alumni with permanent plaques in the 68th Street campus lobby.
cards.evidence_claim: Inductees are listed by year on plaques in the West Lobby at Hunter's 68th Street campus.
cards.source_title: Major League Umpire, Four Other Luminaries Named to Hunter's Hall of Fame
cards.access_notes: The West Lobby is accessible to students and visitors during building hours.

cards.title: Roosevelt House Student Guides
cards.subtitle: Living History Tradition
cards.notes: Student ambassadors lead tours of the former home of FDR and Eleanor Roosevelt, sharing the family's legacy with the public.
cards.short_summary: A student-led tradition of providing historical tours of the Roosevelt House Public Policy Institute.
cards.evidence_claim: Roosevelt House student guides offer tours to visitors at receptions and special events.
cards.source_title: Roosevelt House Student Guides
cards.access_notes: Tours are available by appointment or during scheduled public programs at 47-49 East 65th Street.

cards.title: The Final Confetti Drop
cards.subtitle: Graduation Finale
cards.notes: A celebratory tradition at the end of the Barclays Center commencement ceremony where purple and gold confetti falls on graduates.
cards.short_summary: The traditional finale of the Hunter College commencement ceremony involving a large confetti drop.
cards.evidence_claim: Students wait for confetti to fall at the end of the commencement ceremony.
cards.source_title: What even happens during the graduation ceremony? : r/HunterCollege
cards.access_notes: Occurs annually at the end of the spring commencement ceremony at Barclays Center.

cards.title: The Grotesques of Thomas Hunter
cards.subtitle: Architectural Superstition
cards.notes: The Collegiate Gothic facade of Thomas Hunter Hall features numerous stone grotesques that have watched over students since 1911.
cards.short_summary: The historic stone carvings on Thomas Hunter Hall that serve as a unique architectural tradition.
cards.evidence_claim: Thomas Hunter Hall features numerous grotesques around its façade, along with cathedral-style windows.
cards.source_title: Grotesque faces staring at you at Hunter College | Ephemeral New York
cards.access_notes: Visible from the sidewalk at 934 Lexington Avenue.

cards.title: The Envoy's 80-Year Legacy
cards.subtitle: Student Journalism Tradition
cards.notes: Since 1944, this student-run publication has served as the primary voice for campus news and culture.
cards.short_summary: The long-standing tradition of student-led journalism at Hunter College through The Envoy.
cards.evidence_claim: Since 1944, The Envoy has served as Hunter College's student-run publication.
cards.source_title: Publications and Media - Hunter College - CUNY
cards.access_notes: The publication is distributed across campus and available online.

cards.title: New Student Convocation
cards.subtitle: Official Welcome Ceremony
cards.notes: This required ceremony for freshmen and transfers marks the formal entry into the Hunter academic community each semester.
cards.short_summary: The official welcoming ritual for all new students entering Hunter College.
cards.evidence_claim: New Student Convocation is the official welcome ceremony and celebration exclusively for new students.
cards.source_title: New Student Convocation - Hunter College - CUNY
cards.access_notes: Held at the start of each semester; invitations are sent to student emails.

boards.title: Your First Weekend at CUNY Hunter College, Shared as Cards
boards.description: Navigate the vertical campus and Upper East Side with this guide to your first weekend as a Hunter Hawk.

cards.title: Check In for Orientation
cards.subtitle: 904 Lexington Avenue
cards.notes: Start your weekend by checking in at the corner of 68th and Lexington to receive your visitor pass and orientation materials.
cards.short_summary: The primary entry point for new students and guests to access the main 68th Street campus buildings.
cards.evidence_claim: Guests must check in at the 68th Street Visitors Center at 904 Lexington Avenue to gain access to campus locations like the cafeteria and student center.
cards.source_title: Campus Information - Hunter College
cards.access_notes: Located at the corner of 68th Street and Lexington Avenue.

cards.title: Navigate the Sky Bridges
cards.subtitle: Connecting East, West, and North Buildings
cards.notes: Walk between buildings without hitting the street; the 3rd and 7th floor bridges offer great views of the city skyline.
cards.short_summary: Elevated glass walkways that connect the main campus buildings, essential for navigating the vertical campus.
cards.evidence_claim: Sky bridges connect the East and West buildings on floors 3 and 7, while North and West are connected on the 3rd floor.
cards.source_title: 68th Street Campus Map - Hunter College
cards.access_notes: Accessible to students with a valid Hunter OneCard; bridges are located on floors 3 and 7.

cards.title: Grab Lunch at the Cafeteria
cards.subtitle: West Building, 3rd Floor
cards.notes: Visit the main dining hub for halal-certified dishes, Italian-inspired hot meals, and a full salad bar.
cards.short_summary: The primary campus cafeteria offering diverse food stations including kosher and halal options.
cards.evidence_claim: The Hungry Hawk cafeteria on the third floor features Italian and Spanish-inspired dishes, a dedicated halal station, and grab-and-go kosher meals.
cards.source_title: Hunter Campus To Feature New World of Food Offerings
cards.access_notes: Open during standard campus hours; located on the 3rd floor of the West Building.

cards.title: Find Your Study Spot
cards.subtitle: East Building
cards.notes: Explore the newly renovated 5th floor to find group study rooms equipped with wireless display monitors.
cards.short_summary: The main campus library providing extensive study spaces, technology loans, and research support.
cards.evidence_claim: The Cooperman Library offers reservable group study rooms on the 5th floor equipped with display monitors for student use.
cards.source_title: Study Spaces - Hunter College Libraries
cards.access_notes: Open 8:30am – 8:00pm on weekdays; requires Hunter OneCard for entry.

cards.title: Take a Break in the Park
cards.subtitle: Entrance at 5th Avenue and 68th Street
cards.notes: Walk two blocks west to reach the park; the Conservatory Water area is perfect for watching model boats.
cards.short_summary: A massive urban park located just steps from the Hunter campus, offering a natural escape for students.
cards.evidence_claim: Hunter College is conveniently walking distance from Central Park, which offers free activities like watching model boats at Conservatory Water.
cards.source_title: Children's Activities - Central Park
cards.access_notes: Public park open daily from 6:00am to 1:00am.

cards.title: Meet Peers at the Game Room
cards.subtitle: Thomas Hunter Hall, Room 205
cards.notes: Join Welcome Week events like the Ice Cream Social or Games & Grub to connect with fellow Hawks.
cards.short_summary: A social hub in Thomas Hunter Hall used for student government events and casual recreation.
cards.evidence_claim: The Game Room in Thomas Hunter Hall, Room 205, hosts Welcome Week events like 'Games & Grub' and 'Ice Cream Socials'.
cards.source_title: Welcome Week - Hunter College
cards.access_notes: Located on the 2nd floor of Thomas Hunter Hall; check the student activities calendar for event times.

cards.title: Explore Campus Art
cards.subtitle: West Building Entrance
cards.notes: Visit this gallery to see historical and scholarly exhibitions; it is one of the few campus spaces open to the public.
cards.short_summary: The main campus art gallery featuring rotating exhibitions and BFA degree shows.
cards.evidence_claim: The Bertha and Karl Leubsdorf Gallery is located on the main campus and can be accessed directly through the West Building's entrance.
cards.source_title: Galleries - Art & Art History
cards.access_notes: Open to the public during gallery hours; enter via the West Building.

cards.title: Visit the Fitness Center
cards.subtitle: West Building, B2 Level
cards.notes: Check out the weightlifting facilities and open gym areas to plan your workout routine for the semester.
cards.short_summary: The primary recreation facility for students, offering fitness classes and gym equipment.
cards.evidence_claim: The Fitness Center is located on the B2 Level in the West Building of the Hunter College 68th Street Campus.
cards.source_title: Fitness Center - Facilities
cards.access_notes: Requires a valid Hunter OneCard and a completed fitness waiver for entry.

cards.title: Order Your Textbooks
cards.subtitle: Digital Platform
cards.notes: Use the online portal to compare prices and rent or buy your required course materials before classes start.
cards.short_summary: The official platform for Hunter students to acquire textbooks and academic supplies.
cards.evidence_claim: Students can purchase or rent books and course materials from the online Hunter College Online Bookstore.
cards.source_title: Bookstore Information - Hunter College
cards.access_notes: Accessible 24/7 online; physical pickup locations may vary by semester.

cards.title: Master the Commute
cards.subtitle: Lexington Avenue and 68th Street
cards.notes: Locate the direct campus entrance from the 6 train station to save time on your first day of classes.
cards.short_summary: The primary subway station serving the college, featuring a direct entrance into the North Building.
cards.evidence_claim: The main campus is accessible from the 68th Street - Hunter College stop on the MTA's 6 train.
cards.source_title: Campus Map & Visitor Information
cards.access_notes: Direct entrance to the North Building is available from the subway platform.
